subject: Immediate: Dedicated GPU pool saturation impacting Voyager inference latency & errors
messages:
From: Ethan Wolfe <ewolfe@voyager.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Megan Lee <mlee@voyager.ai>, Voyager SRE <sre@voyager.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: High latency + 5xx spike from Voyager prod (observed 07:30 PST)

Vanessa —

We're seeing a large increase in token latency and a consequential spike in 5xx errors starting around 07:30 PST. P95 went from ~220ms to >1.8s and overall throughput dropped by ~28%. This is affecting our live chat experience. Attached is a short error sample and the SRE traces we pulled (voyager_error_sample.log).

Key points:
- Started ~07:30; sustained for ~45 mins, then intermittent recovery attempts appear to trigger more 5xx.
- Traffic pattern: longer aggregated contexts from a new customer flow rolled out this morning; median input length increased ~2.5x.
- We're on a reserved capacity plan with you (contract DEAL-8742).

Can you confirm whether this is a dedicated pool saturation on your side or something in our integration? We need an initial call and exec-level visibility ASAP — this is customer-impacting.

Thanks,
Ethan
Head of Platform, Voyager.ai

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Ethan Wolfe <ewolfe@voyager.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike from Voyager prod (observed 07:30 PST)

Ethan —

Thanks for the logs and the flags. I'm escalating immediately to our infra and dedicated-pool team (cc'd). We will triage and come back with: 1) root cause hypothesis, 2) immediate mitigations, and 3) short-term capacity/credit asks for Voyager.

I'm proposing a 20-min triage call at 09:00 PST to align on scope; Jonas, Marissa, and David — can you join? If we confirm a saturation/fallback gap, we will need authorization to allocate burst capacity and potentially trigger a limited SLA credit while we remediate.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Voyager SRE <sre@voyager.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike from Voyager prod (observed 07:30 PST)

Quick initial triage notes from infra:
- Observed queue-length climb on the dedicated GPU pool backing Voyager's reservation between 07:28-07:55 PST. Token-generation latencies escalated as batch sizes increased beyond the crafted shedding thresholds.
- KV cache pressure: a new customer flow with longer contexts appears to be inflating KV cache working set; eviction thrashing is causing repeated decoder hot-path stalls.
- We also saw repeated model-variant fallbacks attempted by the runtime (gold -> silver) but an incompatibility in the pinned quantization profile caused additional retries and transient 5xxs.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (fastest to implement):
1) Temporary autotune: reduce max batch size for Voyager's routes from 64 -> 32 (reduces throughput but lowers tail latency).
2) Enable prefix/KV cache pinning for high-context requests to stop eviction churn.
3) Switch Voyager's traffic to the compatible lower-latency variant (rwd-small-8q) as a graceful degraded mode; runtime supports hot-switch with <90s warmup.

If we confirm saturation, the short-term ask will be: authorization to borrow 2x burst capacity from hosted pool for 2 hours and approval for a one-off customer credit (proposal below). I can enact items 1-3 now; need Vanessa/Marissa to approve the customer communication and Jonas for exec sign-off on burst + credits.

-David
David Kim
Director, Serving Infrastructure

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Wolfe <ewolfe@voyager.ai>, Voyager SRE <sre@voyager.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike from Voyager prod (observed 07:30 PST)

On the customer side: Ethan — thanks for the sample. My immediate ask: can your team temporarily gate or reduce the new long-context flow while we apply mitigations? Even a short rollback would help reduce the working set pressure while we apply the fallback.

From a sales/CS perspective, if we do need to offer a credit I recommend: 10% usage credit for the impacted 2-hour window and a commitment to a joint postmortem within 72 hours. We should also offer an ops-runbook link and a pre-scheduled 30-min remediation meeting.

Vanessa — I'm fine with us borrowing hosted burst (2x for 2 hours) to restore customer experience; Jonas, please confirm for exec approval on burst + credit.

-Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Ethan Wolfe <ewolfe@voyager.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike from Voyager prod (observed 07:30 PST)

Thanks team — good write-up. Approve the following immediate actions:
1) Apply David's mitigations 1-3 now.
2) Authorize borrowing 2x hosted burst capacity for up to 3 hours if needed (we'll track actual minutes used to limit cost).
3) Approve the proposed customer credit of 10% for the impacted window, contingent on a root cause analysis and joint postmortem.

Vanessa — please send a short customer note confirming actions and timeline. Also please open an internal incident in PagerDuty with the incident tag and link the runbook.

-Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Ethan Wolfe <ewolfe@voyager.ai>, Megan Lee <mlee@voyager.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Voyager SRE <sre@voyager.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency + 5xx spike from Voyager prod (observed 07:30 PST)

Ethan / Megan —

TL;DR: We identified dedicated-pool saturation driven by longer contexts + KV cache churn and a pinned-quantization mismatch that amplified fallbacks. Immediate steps taken (effective now):
- Reduced max batch size on your routes (64 -> 32).
- Enabled KV cache pinning for high-context flows.
- Warm-switched traffic to rwd-small-8q (degraded variant) to stabilize latency while caches warm.
- Borrowed 2x hosted burst capacity (authorized by Jonas) to absorb spike; will automatically release as metrics normalize.

Customer commitment:
- We propose a 10% usage credit for the impacted 2-hour window.
- Root-cause postmortem with joint findings and remediation plan within 72 hours.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if you can temporarily gate the long-context rollout for 60 minutes to accelerate recovery (Marissa's request).
2) We will share the mutual action plan and postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/Voyager/mutual_action_plan_v1 (attached).

I'm standing by on the remediation call; if you want me to escalate to your CTO or our COO for visibility I can do that immediately.

—Vanessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Attachments: mutual_action_plan_voyager_v1.pdf
